findings.issue_text: P2: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and off-by-one index (substring(3,5) instead of substring(4,6)), making the grant-type assertion vacuous so tests accept tokens minted with the wrong grant type

P2: AccessTokenContext constructor validates grantType twice instead of checking rawTokenId for null, allowing null rawTokenId to flow through encodeTokenId as the literal string "null" and producing a misleading error message

P2: getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException for tokens whose grant shortcut is unknown (e.g., provider removed/disabled or rolling upgrade) instead of degrading gracefully like other unknown-input paths
P3: Context.setFormParams replaces formParams without re-deriving grantType, allowing stale grantType state to be encoded into token ids

P3: GRANT_TYPE attribute set via setAttribute persists as a client-session note under the generic name "grant_type", mutating shared persisted state and being overwritten by the refresh flow on the shared client session
Inverted logic in AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId matcher: returns false when the extracted grant shortcut equals the expected shortcut, making the condition backwards

Wrong substring offsets in AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId: substring(3,5) extracts the last char of tokenType plus first char of grantType instead of the 2-char grant shortcut (chars 5-6), making grant-type assertions vacuous
Copy-paste bug in AccessTokenContext constructor: Objects.requireNonNull(grantType) is called twice and rawTokenId is never null-checked, so a null rawTokenId passes validation

Runtime shortcut-map refresh in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory bypasses the duplicate-shortcut uniqueness validation (only run in postInit), allowing a colliding new grant provider to silently overwrite existing mappings and violate shortcut uniqueness

getTokenContextFromTokenId refresh path inserts entries into shared grantsByShortcuts map from attacker-controllable 2-char shortcut prefixes of client-supplied token IDs, allowing unbounded growth of process-lifetime maps (latent DoS hazard)
Check-then-act on the ConcurrentHashMaps in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut is not atomic, so concurrent first-encounters of colliding grants can interleave inconsistently

P3: Uncacheable cache-miss path in grant-shortcut resolution — unknown shortcut/grant type lookups re-stream all OAuth2GrantTypeFactory instances on every call and misses are never negatively cached, so requests with attacker-supplied unknown shortcuts repeatedly pay the scan
P3: Duplicated null-check in AccessTokenContext constructor — the second Objects.requireNonNull checks grantType again instead of rawTokenId, so rawTokenId can be null silently

P2: Inverted logic and wrong substring indices in AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId — matcher reads items[0].substring(3, 5) instead of the grant shortcut at indices 4–6, and the condition returns false on a match and continues on a mismatch, making the grant-shortcut assertion a no-op and voiding the regression protection of the updated tests

P3: Shortcut-collision validation in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit can silently pass — a third-party grant factory's shortcut colliding with UNKNOWN is silently overwritten by the subsequent put(UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN), producing tokens with misleading context instead of failing fast

Access token `jti` claim format changed unconditionally from plain UUID to composite `<sessionType><tokenType><grantType>:<uuid>` string for all tokens, with no opt-in/opt-out configuration, breaking external consumers that store/key on token IDs and leaking internal session/grant state to token bearers

`getShortcut()` added as a required abstract method on the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` SPI without a default implementation, breaking compilation or runtime loading of existing custom grant providers on upgrade

`isAccessTokenId` test matcher in AssertEvents uses wrong substring indices (`substring(3, 5)` instead of extracting the grantType chars 4-5) and has inverted logic (returns false on match), so grant shortcut is never actually validated and all updated test assertions silently assert nothing about the grant context

`AccessTokenContext` constructor has a copy-paste bug: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...)` is called twice and `rawTokenId` is never null-checked, allowing a null rawTokenId to produce a token ID like `onrtna:null`

Shortcut-collision validation only runs in `postInit`; the lazy `getShortcutByGrantType`/`getGrantTypeByShortcut` refresh paths do `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)` with no collision check, so a later hot-deployed grant with a colliding shortcut silently overwrites the mapping and corrupts grant-type decoding of previously issued tokens

`AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken` changed from instance method to static, causing `IncompatibleClassChangeError` at runtime for previously compiled custom protocol mappers and compile failures for subclasses that overrode it, with no deprecation/bridge provided
Public copy constructor `Context(Context)` removed from `OAuth2GrantType.Context` without deprecation or replacement noted, causing compile errors on upgrade for code that cloned a Context

Inverted matching logic in isAccessTokenId test matcher: returns false when grant shortcut matches and true when it doesn't (AssertEvents.java:481), causing spurious CI failures and silently passing wrong grant shortcuts

Wrong substring offset in the same matcher: code reads substring(3, 5) but the encoded prefix is 6 chars, so no correct token would ever match; inline comment also contradicts the code (AssertEvents.java:480)
Copy/paste error in AccessTokenContext.java:88: second Objects.requireNonNull checks grantType instead of rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId silently passes validation

Unchecked IllegalArgumentException from getTokenContextFromTokenId when parsing externally-supplied token IDs (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74-95); malformed tokens could surface as HTTP 500 instead of clean invalid_token responses

Dynamic shortcut registration in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:110-137) bypasses the duplicate-shortcut validation done in postInit; a runtime-deployed grant with a colliding shortcut silently overwrites the existing mapping

P1: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic AND a wrong substring offset (substring(3,5) instead of indices 4-5), so it accepts any grant type, making all four AssertEvents call-site changes vacuous tests that verify nothing
P1: isAccessTokenId matcher can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when a token id prefix is shorter than 5 chars (e.g. legacy-format id) instead of failing cleanly

P2: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext has zero test coverage — its TRANSIENT/OFFLINE/ONLINE, lightweight-access-token detection, and missing-GRANT_TYPE fallback branches are untested despite being security/behavior-relevant

P2: Tests hand-craft the factory maps bypassing init/postInit, leaving duplicate-shortcut/duplicate-grant-id detection and lazy map-refresh logic untested, and never asserting the real shortcuts (ac, cc, pg, pc, rt, ro, te, ci, dg) are registered and round-trippable via production wiring

P2: No integration/end-to-end coverage of the new token-id format's session-type and token-type dimensions (offline 'of', transient 'tr', lightweight 'lt' vs regular 'rt') nor backward compatibility of old UUID-format token ids through refresh/validation/introspection paths
P3: testIncorrectGrantType swallows any RuntimeException instead of asserting the specific IllegalArgumentException, weakening the test's diagnostic value
P3: Malformed-prefix decode branch in getTokenContextFromTokenId (length check throwing IllegalArgumentException for non-6-char prefixes) is untested
Copy-paste bug: second requireNonNull re-validates grantType instead of rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId silently produces a token ID like 'onrtna:null' (AccessTokenContext.java:80-83)
isAccessTokenId test matcher has wrong offsets (substring(3,5) instead of indices 4-5) and inverted logic, so the grant shortcut is never verified and tests pass vacuously (AssertEvents.java:479-485)

Context.grantType becomes stale if setFormParams is called after construction, since the setter replaces formParams without updating grantType, leading to inconsistent state encoded into token IDs (OAuth2GrantType.java:102, ~104)

GRANT_TYPE attribute setting is scattered across five call sites with no central enforcement, so grants building ClientSessionContext outside createTokenResponse silently encode grant type 'na' (OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java:109, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.java:82, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.java:134, StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java:237, TokenManager.java:248)

Lazy runtime map refresh in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut bypasses the duplicate-shortcut validation done only in postInit, allowing hot-deployed grants with colliding shortcuts to silently overwrite mappings (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:112-137)

Size-based duplicate validation only detects that maps differ, not which grant is at fault, and can be defeated if a grant's id equals another grant's shortcut keeping sizes equal (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:112-137)

Token-ID wire format knowledge (2+2+2 layout, separator, field positions) is duplicated in the test matcher via hardcoded substring offsets instead of delegating to encoder accessors (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:72-98, AssertEvents.java:478-484)

Encoder provider couples to protocol-mapper internals by calling AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken, a cross-package dependency leak requiring the method to be widened to public static (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:66)

Package-private mutable maps grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts exposed solely for the unit test, which bypasses postInit and leaves the duplicate-shortcut validation path with zero coverage (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:45-46)

Constants.GRANT_TYPE is a pure alias for OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE, conflating a session attribute key with a wire parameter name; a distinct purpose-named attribute key would keep the boundary clean (Constants.java:207)

Wrong offsets in isAccessTokenId matcher: substring(3, 5) captures the second char of tokenType and first char of grant, while the grant shortcut actually lives at substring(4, 6) (AssertEvents.java:478-483)
Inverted condition in isAccessTokenId matcher: it returns false (failure) when the extracted chars equal the expected shortcut, when it should fail on mismatch (AssertEvents.java:478-483)

Combined effect of matcher bugs: matcher accepts any 6-char prefix + UUID tail regardless of actual grant encoded, so all grant-type event assertions silently pass and the test safety net verifies nothing (AssertEvents.java:478-483)
Copy-paste bug in AccessTokenContext.java:73-78: grantType is null-checked twice and rawTokenId is never validated, so a null rawTokenId silently produces a token ID of '...:null'

OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) copy constructor deleted from SPI class with no replacement, breaking source and binary compatibility for third-party grant providers (server-spi-private OAuth2GrantType.java)

GRANT_TYPE attribute set on the persisted client session, so the grant_type of the last token request sticks to the session and future tokens issued via paths that don't set the attribute silently inherit a stale grant type (TokenManager.java:248, OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java:109, StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java:237)

encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException if the persisted grant type has no registered provider factory (e.g., a CIBA/Device/OID4VC provider later disabled or removed), causing subsequent token issuance from that client session to fail rather than degrade to 'na' (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:108-120)
Client session note uses the generic key Constants.GRANT_TYPE ('grant_type'), polluting session notes with a key that extensions may assume holds a form parameter

Duplicate-shortcut startup validation is defeatable: a grant registering the reserved shortcut 'na' is overwritten by put(UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN), both maps end up the same size, validation passes, and that grant's tokens permanently mis-decode as 'na' (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:77-99)

Lazy refresh paths getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut write into the maps after validation without collision checks, so two runtime-deployed grants with the same shortcut resolve non-deterministically via unordered findFirst, silently attributing tokens to the wrong grant (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:108-137)

Context.grantType is captured only in the constructor and not updated by setFormParams, so getGrantType() can be stale relative to the actual request form parameters when used to stamp the token prefix (OAuth2GrantType.java:103-111)

getShouldUseLightweightToken is now invoked during initToken and calls session.getContext().getClient().getAttribute(...), risking NPE and failed token issuance from entry points where no client is in the session context; the method was also made public static, inviting more callers into the same trap (TokenManager.java:1051-1053, AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.java:84)

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: AccessTokenContext constructor validates grantType twice instead of checking rawTokenId for null, allowing null rawTokenId to flow through encodeTokenId as the literal string "null" and producing a misleading error message

P2: getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException for tokens whose grant shortcut is unknown (e.g., provider removed/disabled or rolling upgrade) instead of degrading gracefully like other unknown-input paths

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId, after parsing the 6-char context it resolves the grant via factory.getGrantTypeByShortcut(gtShortcut) and explicitly throws IllegalArgumentException when it returns null ("Unknown value ... for grant type"). This means any token whose embedded grant shortcut is not present in the current factory maps (e.g., implementation removed/disabled, rolling upgrade) will hard-fail instead of returning an UNKNOWN-like context (as is done when there is no ':' and via the special 'na' shortcut). The diff shows this behavior is intentional (see test testIncorrectGrantType expecting exception), so it’s more an edge-case/compatibility concern than a clear defect proven by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Context.setFormParams replaces formParams without re-deriving grantType, allowing stale grantType state to be encoded into token ids

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuth2GrantType.Context`, a new cached field `grantType` is derived once in the constructor (`this.grantType = formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE);`). The class still exposes `setFormParams(...)` (shown in the diff) which can change `formParams` after construction, but the diff does not show any corresponding re-derivation of `grantType`. If `setFormParams` is used anywhere to mutate the request parameters, `context.getGrantType()` could become inconsistent with `context.formParams`, and that value is later used to set `clientSessionCtx`'s `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` and ultimately to encode token IDs. However, the diff does not show the body of `setFormParams` nor any call sites, so the defect is a plausible state-consistency concern rather than a verifiable broken behavior from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: GRANT_TYPE attribute set via setAttribute persists as a client-session note under the generic name "grant_type", mutating shared persisted state and being overwritten by the refresh flow on the shared client session

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows multiple calls to `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, ...)` where `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` is `OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE` (i.e., the string "grant_type"). However, nothing in this diff shows that `ClientSessionContext.setAttribute` persists to an underlying client-session note or mutates shared persisted state; the implementation of `setAttribute` is not part of the patch. The refresh flow change in `TokenManager.validateToken` sets the attribute on the `clientSessionCtx` used to recreate the access token, but the claim that this overwrites a shared persisted client session cannot be verified from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inverted logic in AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId matcher: returns false when the extracted grant shortcut equals the expected shortcut, making the condition backwards

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId.matchesSafely, the grant-shortcut check is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects the token ID when the extracted shortcut equals the expected shortcut, so it can never match the intended correct IDs (it should return false when it does NOT equal).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Wrong substring offsets in AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId: substring(3,5) extracts the last char of tokenType plus first char of grantType instead of the 2-char grant shortcut (chars 5-6), making grant-type assertions vacuous

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the encoded token prefix is 6 chars (2 sessionType + 2 tokenType + 2 grant shortcut) per DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(). The grant shortcut is therefore at indices [4,6), but the matcher uses items[0].substring(3, 5), which spans the last char of tokenType and first char of the grant shortcut. Additionally, it returns false when the extracted substring equals expectedGrantShortcut, meaning a correct token would fail the matcher; combined with the wrong substring, this makes the grant-type check effectively meaningless and likely lets tests pass for wrong grant types.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Copy-paste bug in AccessTokenContext constructor: Objects.requireNonNull(grantType) is called twice and rawTokenId is never null-checked, so a null rawTokenId passes validation
matched_golden_ids: In AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth Objects.requireNonNull validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass validation.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same copy-paste bug: grantType is null-checked twice and rawTokenId is not validated, allowing null rawTokenId to pass.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Runtime shortcut-map refresh in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory bypasses the duplicate-shortcut uniqueness validation (only run in postInit), allowing a colliding new grant provider to silently overwrite existing mappings and violate shortcut uniqueness

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() there is a one-time duplicate-shortcut validation via `if (grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size())`, but both runtime refresh paths (`getShortcutByGrantType()` and `getGrantTypeByShortcut()`) can mutate `grantsByShortcuts`/`grantsToShortcuts` with plain `put()` without re-checking collisions. Specifically, `getShortcutByGrantType()` does `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)` and `grantsToShortcuts.put(grantType, shortcut)`; if a newly deployed grant factory returns a shortcut already used by another grant, this will silently overwrite the existing shortcut mapping, violating the intended uniqueness constraint and potentially causing incorrect token-id encoding/decoding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getTokenContextFromTokenId refresh path inserts entries into shared grantsByShortcuts map from attacker-controllable 2-char shortcut prefixes of client-supplied token IDs, allowing unbounded growth of process-lifetime maps (latent DoS hazard)

adjudication.rationale: In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId`, the 2-char `gtShortcut` is attacker-influenced, but `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getGrantTypeByShortcut` only inserts into `grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts` when it finds a matching `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` whose `getShortcut()` equals that shortcut. Arbitrary attacker-provided shortcuts that do not correspond to an installed grant factory are not inserted, so map growth is bounded by the finite set of deployed grant types (plus the constant `na`). The claimed “unbounded growth from attacker-controllable prefixes” is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Check-then-act on the ConcurrentHashMaps in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut is not atomic, so concurrent first-encounters of colliding grants can interleave inconsistently

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, getShortcutByGrantType() and getGrantTypeByShortcut() do a non-atomic “check then refresh then put” on two related ConcurrentHashMaps (grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts), updating them with separate put() calls. This can transiently violate the intended bijection (shortcut<->grant) under concurrent access/refresh, and if a newly deployed grant has a colliding shortcut there’s no runtime enforcement here (only postInit validates the initial set), so concurrent first-seen updates could leave the two maps inconsistent (e.g., shortcut->A while A->shortcut and B->shortcut both exist). The diff shows this pattern; whether it manifests as a user-visible failure depends on runtime deployment/concurrency, so it’s a concrete review concern but not a guaranteed defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Uncacheable cache-miss path in grant-shortcut resolution — unknown shortcut/grant type lookups re-stream all OAuth2GrantTypeFactory instances on every call and misses are never negatively cached, so requests with attacker-supplied unknown shortcuts repeatedly pay the scan

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getGrantTypeByShortcut(String), if grantsByShortcuts.get(shortcut) returns null, the code re-scans all OAuth2GrantType factories via sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class) to try to find a matching shortcut, and only caches on success (ifPresent). If no factory matches, nothing is stored, so the next lookup for the same unknown shortcut will repeat the full stream/scan again. This matches the finding’s “misses are never negatively cached” and can cause repeated costly scans for attacker-supplied unknown shortcuts, though it’s a performance/DoS concern rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Duplicated null-check in AccessTokenContext constructor — the second Objects.requireNonNull checks grantType again instead of rawTokenId, so rawTokenId can be null silently

adjudication.rationale: In the new file `AccessTokenContext.java`, the constructor performs `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of checking `rawTokenId`. This duplicated null-check means `rawTokenId` can be null without being rejected, contrary to the apparent intent and the error message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Inverted logic and wrong substring indices in AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId — matcher reads items[0].substring(3, 5) instead of the grant shortcut at indices 4–6, and the condition returns false on a match and continues on a mismatch, making the grant-shortcut assertion a no-op and voiding the regression protection of the updated tests

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the encoded context format elsewhere in the diff is 6 chars: sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantShortcut(2) (see DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId). Therefore the grant shortcut should be extracted with substring(4, 6), not substring(3, 5). Additionally, the matcher returns false when the extracted substring equals the expected shortcut (`if (...) return false;`), which inverts the intended assertion; on mismatch it proceeds to only validate the UUID part, effectively making the grant-shortcut check ineffective. This is a real, diff-verifiable correctness defect in the updated tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Shortcut-collision validation in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit can silently pass — a third-party grant factory's shortcut colliding with UNKNOWN is silently overwritten by the subsequent put(UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN), producing tokens with misleading context instead of failing fast

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit, a third-party grant using shortcut "na" (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.UNKNOWN) would be overwritten by the later grantsByShortcuts.put("na","na"), but this does *not* silently pass: grantsByShortcuts size would stay the same while grantsToShortcuts gains a new key ("na"), so the subsequent size check (grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size()) would throw IllegalStateException and fail fast. Only an extreme case where both the grant shortcut *and* the grant id are "na" could avoid the size mismatch, which the finding does not claim and is not implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Access token `jti` claim format changed unconditionally from plain UUID to composite `<sessionType><tokenType><grantType>:<uuid>` string for all tokens, with no opt-in/opt-out configuration, breaking external consumers that store/key on token IDs and leaking internal session/grant state to token bearers

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the access token ID (jti) is no longer always a plain UUID: `TokenManager.initToken` now builds an `AccessTokenContext` and sets `token.id(encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx))`, where `encodeTokenId` concatenates `<sessionType><tokenType><grantShortcut> + ':' + <rawUuid>` (e.g., `onrtcc:...`). This is applied unconditionally for newly created access tokens (no feature flag/opt-out in the shown code path), and it does embed session/token/grant metadata into the token ID. However, the claim that this definitively “breaks external consumers” can’t be verified from the diff itself (that depends on external integrations), so it’s best treated as a compatibility/architecture concern rather than a provable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `getShortcut()` added as a required abstract method on the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` SPI without a default implementation, breaking compilation or runtime loading of existing custom grant providers on upgrade

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut();` to the public SPI interface `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` with no default implementation. Any existing (external/custom) `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations that are not updated will fail to compile against this version, and even already-compiled providers will hit runtime linkage errors when Keycloak calls `gtf.getShortcut()` (see `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` iterating all `OAuth2GrantType` factories and invoking `getShortcut()`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `isAccessTokenId` test matcher in AssertEvents uses wrong substring indices (`substring(3, 5)` instead of extracting the grantType chars 4-5) and has inverted logic (returns false on match), so grant shortcut is never actually validated and all updated test assertions silently assert nothing about the grant context

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the matcher extracts the grant shortcut with `items[0].substring(3, 5)`, but the encoded context is 6 chars where grantType is the last 2 chars (0-based indices 4–5), so it should be `substring(4, 6)`. Additionally, the logic is inverted: `if ( ... .equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects the expected value instead of accepting it. Combined, this means the matcher typically never validates the grant shortcut (it will just check the UUID after `:`), so the updated event assertions don’t actually assert the grant context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `AccessTokenContext` constructor has a copy-paste bug: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...)` is called twice and `rawTokenId` is never null-checked, allowing a null rawTokenId to produce a token ID like `onrtna:null`

adjudication.rationale: In the new `AccessTokenContext` constructor, `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...)` is invoked twice, and `rawTokenId` is never checked (`Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` is a copy/paste error). This allows constructing an `AccessTokenContext` with `rawTokenId == null`, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` would then concatenate `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()` producing an encoded token id ending in `:null`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Shortcut-collision validation only runs in `postInit`; the lazy `getShortcutByGrantType`/`getGrantTypeByShortcut` refresh paths do `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)` with no collision check, so a later hot-deployed grant with a colliding shortcut silently overwrites the mapping and corrupts grant-type decoding of previously issued tokens

adjudication.rationale: In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory`, duplicate-shortcut validation is only performed in `postInit()` by comparing `grantsByShortcuts.size()` vs `grantsToShortcuts.size()`. However, both lazy refresh paths can mutate the maps without any collision detection: `getShortcutByGrantType()` does `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)` / `grantsToShortcuts.put(grantType, shortcut)` and `getGrantTypeByShortcut()` does `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, newGrantType)` / `grantsToShortcuts.put(newGrantType, shortcut)`. If a newly available ("deployed") grant type reuses an existing shortcut, these `put` calls can silently overwrite an existing mapping, changing how previously issued token IDs decode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken` changed from instance method to static, causing `IncompatibleClassChangeError` at runtime for previously compiled custom protocol mappers and compile failures for subclasses that overrode it, with no deprecation/bridge provided

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(KeycloakSession)` from an instance method to a `public static` method (`boolean getShouldUseLightweightToken(...)` -> `public static boolean getShouldUseLightweightToken(...)`). This is a binary-incompatible change: previously compiled code that invoked it virtually (or subclasses in the same package that overrode it) would no longer link/compile as before, and no instance-method bridge/deprecation is added in the diff to preserve compatibility.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public copy constructor `Context(Context)` removed from `OAuth2GrantType.Context` without deprecation or replacement noted, causing compile errors on upgrade for code that cloned a Context

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor from `org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.OAuth2GrantType.Context` (the entire constructor block is deleted), with no deprecation or alternative cloning mechanism added. While this is not a functional/runtime defect by itself, it is a concrete SPI/API compatibility break that could cause downstream compile failures for any code previously using `new Context(existingContext)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inverted matching logic in isAccessTokenId test matcher: returns false when grant shortcut matches and true when it doesn't (AssertEvents.java:481), causing spurious CI failures and silently passing wrong grant shortcuts

adjudication.rationale: The new AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false when the grant shortcut matches, and otherwise returns `isUUID().matches(items[1])`, so it can incorrectly pass when the shortcut does NOT match. Additionally, given the token id prefix is 6 chars (2 session + 2 token + 2 grant), the grant shortcut should start at index 4 (substring(4,6)), but the code uses substring(3,5), which is off by one.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Wrong substring offset in the same matcher: code reads substring(3, 5) but the encoded prefix is 6 chars, so no correct token would ever match; inline comment also contradicts the code (AssertEvents.java:480)

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(), the token-id prefix format encoded by DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId() is 6 chars: sessionType(2)+tokenType(2)+grantShortcut(2), then ':' (e.g., "trltcc:1234"). Therefore the grant shortcut occupies indices [4,6) of items[0], but the matcher uses items[0].substring(3, 5), which is off by one and contradicts the comment. Additionally, the logic is inverted: if the substring equals the expected shortcut it returns false, so even correctly formatted token IDs would fail to match.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Copy/paste error in AccessTokenContext.java:88: second Objects.requireNonNull checks grantType instead of rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId silently passes validation

adjudication.rationale: In the new `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the 4th validation line is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` instead of checking `rawTokenId`. This means `rawTokenId` can be null without triggering validation, and the error message is misleading. This is a concrete copy/paste correctness defect visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unchecked IllegalArgumentException from getTokenContextFromTokenId when parsing externally-supplied token IDs (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74-95); malformed tokens could surface as HTTP 500 instead of clean invalid_token responses

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId, malformed/unknown encoded token IDs explicitly throw IllegalArgumentException (e.g., encodedContext.length()!=6 or unknown shortcuts). The diff does not show any caller that catches/mapping these exceptions to an OAuth-style invalid_token response, so the concern about needing defensive handling is valid, but whether it actually becomes an HTTP 500 is not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dynamic shortcut registration in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:110-137) bypasses the duplicate-shortcut validation done in postInit; a runtime-deployed grant with a colliding shortcut silently overwrites the existing mapping

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() the code validates uniqueness of shortcuts by comparing grantsByShortcuts.size() vs grantsToShortcuts.size() after initially loading all OAuth2GrantTypeFactory instances. However, both getShortcutByGrantType() and getGrantTypeByShortcut() later “refresh” the mappings by doing unconditional puts into grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts (e.g., grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType) / grantsToShortcuts.put(grantType, shortcut)) without any collision check. If a newly available/runtime-deployed grant uses an existing shortcut, the put into grantsByShortcuts will overwrite the previous mapping for that shortcut, effectively bypassing the duplicate-shortcut validation done in postInit and causing incorrect grantType<->shortcut resolution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic AND a wrong substring offset (substring(3,5) instead of indices 4-5), so it accepts any grant type, making all four AssertEvents call-site changes vacuous tests that verify nothing

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the matcher returns false when the extracted shortcut *equals* the expected shortcut (`if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`), which is inverted logic (it should fail when it does NOT equal). Additionally, the grant shortcut in the encoded token id is the 3rd 2-char segment (sessionType[0-2], tokenType[2-4], grant[4-6]), so the correct slice should be `substring(4,6)`, not `substring(3,5)`. As written, it will generally accept tokens regardless of grant type (only requiring the part after ':' be a UUID), making the updated expectations in call sites effectively non-verifying.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: isAccessTokenId matcher can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when a token id prefix is shorter than 5 chars (e.g. legacy-format id) instead of failing cleanly

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, after checking only `items.length != 2`, it unconditionally calls `items[0].substring(3, 5)`. If the token id contains a ':' but the prefix before it is shorter than 5 characters, this will throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning false. The diff adds this matcher with no length guard on `items[0]`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext has zero test coverage — its TRANSIENT/OFFLINE/ONLINE, lightweight-access-token detection, and missing-GRANT_TYPE fallback branches are untested despite being security/behavior-relevant

adjudication.rationale: The new method DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider#getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...) contains nontrivial branching logic (sessionType based on UserSessionModel persistence/offline, tokenType via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), and GRANT_TYPE attribute fallback to UNKNOWN). In the added test class DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest, only getTokenContextFromTokenId(...) and encodeTokenId(...) are exercised; there are no tests constructing a ClientSessionContext/UserSessionModel to cover TRANSIENT/OFFLINE/ONLINE, lightweight vs regular detection, or missing GRANT_TYPE fallback in getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext. This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Tests hand-craft the factory maps bypassing init/postInit, leaving duplicate-shortcut/duplicate-grant-id detection and lazy map-refresh logic untested, and never asserting the real shortcuts (ac, cc, pg, pc, rt, ro, te, ci, dg) are registered and round-trippable via production wiring

adjudication.rationale: The new production logic for grant shortcut registration/validation lives in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(): it populates grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts from OAuth2GrantType factories, validates duplicate shortcuts via size mismatch, and includes lazy refresh in getShortcutByGrantType()/getGrantTypeByShortcut(). However, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before() manually assigns factory.grantsByShortcuts and factory.grantsToShortcuts and never calls postInit(), so it does not exercise the duplicate-shortcut detection, the provider-factory discovery/registration of real shortcuts (ac, cc, pg, pc, rt, ro, te, ci, dg), or the lazy refresh paths. This is a concrete coverage gap tied to the diff, not a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: No integration/end-to-end coverage of the new token-id format's session-type and token-type dimensions (offline 'of', transient 'tr', lightweight 'lt' vs regular 'rt') nor backward compatibility of old UUID-format token ids through refresh/validation/introspection paths

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new access-token ID encoding (TokenManager.initToken now uses TokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId) that embeds sessionType/tokenType/grantType shortcuts, and adds only a unit test (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest) that covers parsing/encoding and the “old token” case (no ':'). The integration-level changes shown (AssertEvents now expects isAccessTokenId(...)) validate only that the raw-id part is a UUID and attempt to validate grant shortcut, but do not exercise or assert the session-type ('of'/'tr' etc.) or token-type ('lt'/'rt') dimensions end-to-end, nor do they cover backwards-compatibility behavior through refresh/validation/introspection flows. From the diff, there is no E2E/integration coverage of those dimensions beyond the isolated unit test of the encoder/decoder.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: testIncorrectGrantType swallows any RuntimeException instead of asserting the specific IllegalArgumentException, weakening the test's diagnostic value
matched_golden_ids: Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag that the test catches a broad RuntimeException, which hides the specific failure type, and should instead assert/catch the specific IllegalArgumentException thrown by the implementation for more precise diagnostics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Malformed-prefix decode branch in getTokenContextFromTokenId (length check throwing IllegalArgumentException for non-6-char prefixes) is untested

adjudication.rationale: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() has an explicit branch that throws IllegalArgumentException when the prefix before ':' is not length 6 ("if (encodedContext.length() != 6) { throw ... }"). The added unit test DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest covers: no-colon legacy token ("1234"), unknown grant shortcut ("onrtna:5678"), and unknown grant shortcut mapped to exception via factory ("ofrtac:5678"), but it does not include any case like "onrtroX:123" or "onrt:123" that triggers the non-6-length prefix exception branch. This is a specific missing-test gap for newly added parsing/validation logic, not a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Copy-paste bug: second requireNonNull re-validates grantType instead of rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId silently produces a token ID like 'onrtna:null' (AccessTokenContext.java:80-83)

adjudication.rationale: In AccessTokenContext constructor, the last null-check mistakenly calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of validating `rawTokenId` (new file AccessTokenContext.java). This allows `rawTokenId` to be null without throwing, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` will then concatenate `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`, yielding an encoded token id ending with ":null".

adjudication_records.issue_text: isAccessTokenId test matcher has wrong offsets (substring(3,5) instead of indices 4-5) and inverted logic, so the grant shortcut is never verified and tests pass vacuously (AssertEvents.java:479-485)

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the token ID format introduced/used elsewhere is 6 chars before ':' (2 sessionType + 2 tokenType + 2 grant shortcut), so the grant shortcut should be extracted with substring(4,6). The matcher uses substring(3,5), which spans the last char of tokenType and first char of grant shortcut, making equality with a 2-char shortcut effectively impossible. Additionally, the logic is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects the expected shortcut rather than requiring it. As a result, the matcher will typically just validate the UUID part and not actually verify the grant shortcut, letting tests pass without checking the intended condition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Context.grantType becomes stale if setFormParams is called after construction, since the setter replaces formParams without updating grantType, leading to inconsistent state encoded into token IDs (OAuth2GrantType.java:102, ~104)

adjudication.rationale: In OAuth2GrantType.Context, `grantType` is initialized once in the constructor from `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)`, but `setFormParams(...)` (still present) can later replace `this.formParams` without updating `this.grantType`. Since `OAuth2GrantTypeBase` now persists `context.getGrantType()` into `ClientSessionContext` (`clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType())`) and token IDs are encoded from that attribute, calling `setFormParams` after construction can indeed leave `grantType` inconsistent/stale relative to the current form params.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GRANT_TYPE attribute setting is scattered across five call sites with no central enforcement, so grants building ClientSessionContext outside createTokenResponse silently encode grant type 'na' (OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java:109, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.java:82, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.java:134, StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java:237, TokenManager.java:248)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the new token-id encoding depends on `ClientSessionContext` attribute `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` (set in several places: `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse` adds `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType())`, and there are additional explicit sets in `PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType`, `ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType`, `StandardTokenExchangeProvider`, and `TokenManager.validateToken` for refresh). `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` falls back to `UNKNOWN`/`"na"` when the attribute is missing. There is no single central enforcement in `TokenManager.initToken` itself to ensure the attribute is always present for every access-token creation path, so any other (not shown) access-token issuance path that doesn’t set it will encode `na`. This is a real architectural/coverage concern grounded in the diff, but not a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone because the `na` fallback is intentional and no specific missing call site is demonstrated here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Lazy runtime map refresh in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut bypasses the duplicate-shortcut validation done only in postInit, allowing hot-deployed grants with colliding shortcuts to silently overwrite mappings (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:112-137)

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() duplicate shortcut validation is only performed once by comparing grantsByShortcuts.size() vs grantsToShortcuts.size(). However, both getShortcutByGrantType() and getGrantTypeByShortcut() lazily refresh the maps on cache miss and unconditionally put into grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts without re-checking collisions. Because grantsByShortcuts is keyed by shortcut, a newly discovered/hot-deployed grant with a shortcut already in use would overwrite the existing mapping (grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)) and no error is raised, bypassing the earlier uniqueness validation and potentially causing ambiguous/incorrect token-id decoding/encoding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Size-based duplicate validation only detects that maps differ, not which grant is at fault, and can be defeated if a grant's id equals another grant's shortcut keeping sizes equal (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:112-137)

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), duplicate detection is implemented only as `if (grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size())` after populating the two maps from `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getId()` and `getShortcut()`. This check does not identify which grant caused the collision, and it can miss invalid configurations when collisions happen in both dimensions (e.g., one duplicated shortcut overwrites an entry in `grantsByShortcuts` while a duplicated grant id overwrites an entry in `grantsToShortcuts`, keeping sizes equal). The finding’s specific example about “id equals another grant’s shortcut” isn’t directly what the size check is comparing, but the broader concern about size-based validation being insufficient is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Token-ID wire format knowledge (2+2+2 layout, separator, field positions) is duplicated in the test matcher via hardcoded substring offsets instead of delegating to encoder accessors (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:72-98, AssertEvents.java:478-484)

adjudication.rationale: The test matcher `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId` hardcodes token-id field positions (`items[0].substring(3, 5)`) instead of using the encoder/parser logic in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` (which defines the 2+2+2 layout via substrings 0-2, 2-4, 4-6). This duplication has already diverged: grant-type shortcut should be at indices 4-6, but the test uses 3-5, and it also returns `false` when the substring equals the expected shortcut (`if (...) return false;`). As a result, correct encoded token IDs will not match, breaking/invalidating the tests introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Encoder provider couples to protocol-mapper internals by calling AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken, a cross-package dependency leak requiring the method to be widened to public static (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:66)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider calling AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session) (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java), and AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper was changed from a package-private instance method to a public static method specifically to allow that call (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/mappers/AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.java). This introduces a cross-package dependency from the new token-id encoder SPI onto protocol-mapper internals, which is an architecture/design concern rather than a directly verifiable functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Package-private mutable maps grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts exposed solely for the unit test, which bypasses postInit and leaves the duplicate-shortcut validation path with zero coverage (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:45-46)

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory the fields `grantsByShortcuts` and `grantsToShortcuts` are declared with no access modifier (package-private) and are mutated directly by the unit test (`factory.grantsByShortcuts = new HashMap<>(); ... factory.grantsToShortcuts = ...`). The test also only calls `init(null)` and never exercises `postInit(...)`, where the duplicate-shortcut validation lives (`if (grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size()) throw ...`). This is a concrete design/testability concern introduced by the diff: internal mutable state is exposed to make the test work, and the validation logic path is not covered by that test setup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Constants.GRANT_TYPE is a pure alias for OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE, conflating a session attribute key with a wire parameter name; a distinct purpose-named attribute key would keep the boundary clean (Constants.java:207)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Constants.GRANT_TYPE = OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE` (Constants.java), and then uses `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` as a `ClientSessionContext` attribute key in multiple places (e.g., TokenManager refresh flow and OAuth2GrantTypeBase#createTokenResponse). Since `OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE` is the OAuth2 wire/form parameter name (`grant_type`), reusing it as an internal session-attribute key does conflate two concerns/namespaces. This is an architectural/boundary cleanliness issue rather than a directly verifiable functional defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Wrong offsets in isAccessTokenId matcher: substring(3, 5) captures the second char of tokenType and first char of grant, while the grant shortcut actually lives at substring(4, 6) (AssertEvents.java:478-483)

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(), the encoded context is 6 chars: sessionType(0-2) + tokenType(2-4) + grant(4-6). Therefore the grant shortcut occupies substring(4, 6). AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId() uses items[0].substring(3, 5), which spans the last char of tokenType (index 3) and first char of grant (index 4), so it cannot correctly match the 2-char grant shortcut.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inverted condition in isAccessTokenId matcher: it returns false (failure) when the extracted chars equal the expected shortcut, when it should fail on mismatch (AssertEvents.java:478-483)

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the matcher inverts the grant-shortcut check: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` causes a failure when the extracted shortcut *matches* the expected value, instead of failing on mismatch. This is directly visible in the added code at the end of AssertEvents.java. (Additionally, given the encoding described elsewhere in the diff, the substring indices look suspect, but the reported inverted condition is clearly a real defect.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: Combined effect of matcher bugs: matcher accepts any 6-char prefix + UUID tail regardless of actual grant encoded, so all grant-type event assertions silently pass and the test safety net verifies nothing (AssertEvents.java:478-483)

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(), the matcher logic is incorrect: it does `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` and otherwise only checks `isUUID().matches(items[1])`. This both (a) uses wrong indices for the grant shortcut (should be chars 4-5 in a 6-char prefix, i.e., substring(4,6), not substring(3,5)), and (b) inverts the condition (it returns false when it "matches"). Net effect: for typical encoded IDs (e.g., `trltcc:...`), `substring(3,5)` rarely equals the expected grant shortcut, so the matcher accepts almost any `<prefix>:<uuid>` regardless of actual grant encoding, making the event assertions ineffective.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Copy-paste bug in AccessTokenContext.java:73-78: grantType is null-checked twice and rawTokenId is never validated, so a null rawTokenId silently produces a token ID of '...:null'

adjudication.rationale: In the new AccessTokenContext constructor, rawTokenId is never null-checked: it calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of checking rawTokenId (lines shown around the constructor). As a result, AccessTokenContext can be created with rawTokenId == null, and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId() will concatenate ':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId(), yielding an encoded token id ending with ":null".

adjudication_records.issue_text: OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) copy constructor deleted from SPI class with no replacement, breaking source and binary compatibility for third-party grant providers (server-spi-private OAuth2GrantType.java)

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the public copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` from `server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java` (it is deleted entirely) and does not add any replacement overload with equivalent signature/behavior. Since `OAuth2GrantType.Context` is part of the server-spi-private SPI surface for grant implementations, any third-party code that previously called this constructor will fail to compile (source incompatibility) and any already-compiled code will fail to link at runtime with `NoSuchMethodError` (binary incompatibility). The only related addition is a new `grantType` field and getter populated from `formParams`, which does not replace the removed constructor.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GRANT_TYPE attribute set on the persisted client session, so the grant_type of the last token request sticks to the session and future tokens issued via paths that don't set the attribute silently inherit a stale grant type (TokenManager.java:248, OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java:109, StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java:237)

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, ...)` on `ClientSessionContext` (e.g., TokenManager refresh flow, OAuth2GrantTypeBase, StandardTokenExchangeProvider). From the diff alone, there is no evidence this attribute is persisted onto the underlying client session across requests (as a note) such that it would “stick” and be reused later. Also, the new encoder explicitly falls back to `UNKNOWN` when the attribute is missing (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext`), which contradicts the claim of silently inheriting a stale value unless persistence is proven elsewhere (not shown in this PR).

adjudication_records.issue_text: encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException if the persisted grant type has no registered provider factory (e.g., a CIBA/Device/OID4VC provider later disabled or removed), causing subsequent token issuance from that client session to fail rather than degrade to 'na' (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:108-120)

adjudication.rationale: Verified in the diff: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId() calls factory.getShortcutByGrantType(tokenContext.getGrantType()) and throws IllegalStateException when it returns null (services/.../DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:~99-106). DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getShortcutByGrantType() only populates the mapping if a matching OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is currently registered; if the grant type string is present in ClientSessionContext but its provider factory is no longer available (disabled/removed), the lookup stays null and token id encoding fails (services/.../DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:~108-120). There is no fallback to the 'na' shortcut in this case (only when grantType attribute is null), so token issuance can fail due to this metadata encoding step.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client session note uses the generic key Constants.GRANT_TYPE ('grant_type'), polluting session notes with a key that extensions may assume holds a form parameter

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Constants.GRANT_TYPE = OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE` (i.e., the literal string `"grant_type"`) and then persists it into `ClientSessionContext` via `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, ...)` in multiple flows (e.g., `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse`, `ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.process`, `TokenManager.validateToken` refresh path, `StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient`, `PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.process`). This does add a very generic key name into session context storage, which could collide with or be assumed by extensions to represent the original incoming form parameter rather than a stored note/attribute. The diff itself doesn’t prove a concrete breakage, but it does create a specific namespace/architecture concern grounded in the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate-shortcut startup validation is defeatable: a grant registering the reserved shortcut 'na' is overwritten by put(UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN), both maps end up the same size, validation passes, and that grant's tokens permanently mis-decode as 'na' (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:77-99)

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), a grant using shortcut "na" would be inserted into grantsByShortcuts during the provider-factory scan, but the subsequent grantsByShortcuts.put(UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN) would overwrite that key while grantsToShortcuts.put(UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN) would *add* a new key (since the grant’s ID is not "na"), making the map sizes differ and triggering the intended IllegalStateException. The finding’s claim that “both maps end up the same size, validation passes” is not supported by the diff unless a grant also (implausibly) uses ID "na", in which case decoding to "na" would match its own ID anyway.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Lazy refresh paths getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut write into the maps after validation without collision checks, so two runtime-deployed grants with the same shortcut resolve non-deterministically via unordered findFirst, silently attributing tokens to the wrong grant (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:108-137)

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, postInit() validates duplicate shortcuts only for the initially discovered factories, but the lazy refresh paths in getShortcutByGrantType() and getGrantTypeByShortcut() later mutate grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts via put() without any collision/uniqueness checks. In particular, getGrantTypeByShortcut() uses getProviderFactoriesStream(...).filter(...).findFirst() (order not defined) and then puts the mapping, so if multiple runtime-available grants share a shortcut, resolution can be non-deterministic and/or overwrite an existing shortcut->grant mapping, leading to incorrect decoding/encoding of token IDs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Context.grantType is captured only in the constructor and not updated by setFormParams, so getGrantType() can be stale relative to the actual request form parameters when used to stamp the token prefix (OAuth2GrantType.java:103-111)

adjudication.rationale: In OAuth2GrantType.Context, the new field `grantType` is initialized once in the constructor via `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)` and exposed via `getGrantType()`. The existing `setFormParams(...)` method (still present in the diff) does not update `grantType`, so if any code path mutates the context’s form params after construction, `getGrantType()` can diverge from the current `formParams`. The diff doesn’t show a concrete call site where `setFormParams` changes `grant_type`, so the stale-value impact is plausible but not directly verifiable as a runtime defect from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getShouldUseLightweightToken is now invoked during initToken and calls session.getContext().getClient().getAttribute(...), risking NPE and failed token issuance from entry points where no client is in the session context; the method was also made public static, inviting more callers into the same trap (TokenManager.java:1051-1053, AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.java:84)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new call path to `AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)` from `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...)` during `TokenManager.initToken(...)` (new token-id encoding). `getShouldUseLightweightToken` (now `public static`) dereferences `session.getContext().getClient().getAttribute(...)` without a null check. The diff does not show `TokenManager.initToken` ensuring `session.getContext().setClient(client)` before invoking the encoder, so if token issuance happens on a code path where the session context client is unset, this will throw an NPE and break token issuance. Making the method `public static` also increases the surface for the same null-dereference pitfall.
